headline: 3 nomination papers filed for Presidential Election in Bangladesh
summary: BNP's Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and 11-party alliance candidate Oli Ahmed are contesting the 23rd presidential race.
details: Three nomination papers were submitted to the Election Commission (EC) by the final deadline on Thursday, August 13, for the 23rd presidential election.
BNP candidate Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir filed one nomination paper, while Oli Ahmed, representing an 11-party alliance, filed two nomination papers.
EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed confirmed the details during a press conference, noting that the second nomination paper for Oli Ahmed serves as a backup if the first is rejected.
Oli Ahmed's first nomination paper was submitted by opposition leader and Jamaat-e-Islami's Amir Shafiqur Rahman and supported by NCP's Abdullah Al Amin.

The second nomination paper for the 11-party alliance candidate was filed by Jamaat's Assistant Secretary General Rafiqul Islam Khan, with NCP's Mahmuda Mitu as proposer and Jamaat's Abdul Baten as seconder.
According to the schedule, nomination papers will be scrutinized on August 16, and the final date for withdrawal of candidacy is August 18.
Voting will take place on August 20 in the National Parliament, where members of parliament will be candidates' votes.
Due to multiple candidates, a vote will be required for the first time in 35 years. However, as the BNP holds a two-thirds majority in parliament, Mirza Fakhrul is widely seen as the certain winner.
caption:
For the first time in 35 years, Bangladesh will hold a presidential vote in Parliament. Three nomination papers have been filed for the 23rd presidential race.

Three nomination papers were submitted to the Election Commission (EC) by the final deadline on Thursday, August 13, for the 23rd presidential election.

BNP candidate Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir filed one nomination paper, while Oli Ahmed, representing an 11-party alliance, filed two nomination papers.

EC Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed confirmed the details during a press conference, noting that the second nomination paper for Oli Ahmed serves as a backup if the first is rejected.

Oli Ahmed's first nomination paper was submitted by opposition leader and Jamaat-e-Islami's Amir Shafiqur Rahman and supported by NCP's Abdullah Al Amin.

The second nomination paper for the 11-party alliance candidate was filed by Jamaat's Assistant Secretary General Rafiqul Islam Khan, with NCP's Mahmuda Mitu as proposer and Jamaat's Abdul Baten as seconder.

According to the schedule, nomination papers will be scrutinized on August 16, and the final date for withdrawal of candidacy is August 18.

Voting will take place on August 20 in the National Parliament, where members of parliament will be candidates' votes.

Due to multiple candidates, a vote will be required for the first time in 35 years. However, as the BNP holds a two-thirds majority in parliament, Mirza Fakhrul is widely seen as the certain winner.

headline_marked: Hasan Mahmud's 6-wicket haul: [[Bangladesh bowl out Australia for 198]] in Darwin
headline: Hasan Mahmud's 6-wicket haul: Bangladesh bowl out Australia for 198 in Darwin
summary: Hasan Mahmud's career-best 6-55 dismantles Australia, marking their lowest Test total ever against Bangladesh.
details: Hasan Mahmud delivered a career-best 6-55 to bowl out Australia for 198 on Day 1 of the Test in Darwin, giving Bangladesh a commanding start.
This performance marks the first time a Bangladesh bowler has taken a five-wicket haul in Australia across all formats, and it is Australia's lowest Test total against the Tigers.
Hasan is now the third Bangladesh bowler to achieve a five-for against Australia, joining Mohammad Rafique and Shakib Al Hasan.
Bangladesh's pacers took all 10 wickets in the innings, a feat they have only achieved twice in their Test history.
Bangladesh ended the day at 96-1, trailing by 102 runs, with Mominul Haque unbeaten on 35 and Tanzid Hasan on 32.
In a historic milestone, Mominul Haque surpassed Tamim Iqbal to become Bangladesh's second-highest Test run-scorer, trailing only Mushfiqur Rahim.
On the Australian side, Mitchell Starc became the most successful left-arm bowler in Test history, surpassing Rangana Herath.
Steve Smith also reached a milestone, recording his 82nd Test fifty-plus score, joining Steve Waugh on Australia's all-time list.
caption:
Hasan Mahmud's 6-wicket masterclass! 🇧🇩 Australia bowled out for 198—their lowest ever against Bangladesh.

Hasan Mahmud delivered a career-best 6-55 to bowl out Australia for 198 on Day 1 of the Test in Darwin, giving Bangladesh a commanding start.

This performance marks the first time a Bangladesh bowler has taken a five-wicket haul in Australia across all formats, and it is Australia's lowest Test total against the Tigers.

Hasan is now the third Bangladesh bowler to achieve a five-for against Australia, joining Mohammad Rafique and Shakib Al Hasan.

Bangladesh's pacers took all 10 wickets in the innings, a feat they have only achieved twice in their Test history.

Bangladesh ended the day at 96-1, trailing by 102 runs, with Mominul Haque unbeaten on 35 and Tanzid Hasan on 32.

In a historic milestone, Mominul Haque surpassed Tamim Iqbal to become Bangladesh's second-highest Test run-scorer, trailing only Mushfiqur Rahim.

On the Australian side, Mitchell Starc became the most successful left-arm bowler in Test history, surpassing Rangana Herath.

Steve Smith also reached a milestone, recording his 82nd Test fifty-plus score, joining Steve Waugh on Australia's all-time list.
